name: Bosporus
genZNote: The Bosporus runs right through the middle of Istanbul — it's probably the only major shipping chokepoint you can watch from a city café.

sections.heading: 🚨 Location & What It Connects
bullets: A natural strait running through Istanbul, Turkey, separating Europe from Asia.
Connects the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara, which then connects (via the Dardanelles) to the Aegean Sea and the wider Mediterranean.
One of the narrowest straits used for major international shipping anywhere in the world.

sections.heading: ⚓ Why It Matters
bullets: The only sea route in or out of the Black Sea — all Black Sea-region trade (Russian and Ukrainian grain, oil, and other goods) must pass through it.
Runs directly through a major city (Istanbul), making navigation and safety management especially complex compared to most other chokepoints.
Governed by the Montreux Convention (1936), an international treaty regulating naval passage through the strait.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The Bosporus is a narrow strait through Istanbul connecting the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara, the only sea route out of the Black Sea.
keyFacts: Runs through Istanbul, Turkey; separates Europe and Asia.
Connects the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara.
Only sea outlet from the Black Sea.
commonConfusion: The Bosporus and the Dardanelles are two separate straits with the Sea of Marmara between them — together they form the Black Sea's route to the Mediterranean.

highYieldFacts: Bosporus = Istanbul strait connecting Black Sea ↔ Sea of Marmara.
Only sea route out of the Black Sea.
commonTraps: Don't confuse the order: Black Sea → Bosporus → Sea of Marmara → Dardanelles → Mediterranean/Aegean.
mustRemember: Bosporus = Black Sea's only exit, runs through Istanbul, governed by the Montreux Convention.
